bbs_physics.config.title: Physics
bbs_physics.config.general.title: General
bbs_physics.config.general.enabled-comme: The master switch of the physics engine. With it off, nothing is simulated and the addon costs nothing.
bbs_physics.config.general.debug-comment: Draws the shapes the simulation actually works with, on top of the rendered scene.
bbs_physics.config.general.collision_pre: Draws collision over the model in the form editor, so shapes can be placed by eye.
bbs_physics.config.general.world_radius-: How much of the world around the scene takes part in physics. Past that edge there is nothing to land on and a body falls forever. Larger is safer and costs more to assemble.
bbs_physics.config.general.world_below-c: How deep under the scene the ground is collected. Too little and anything going over a ledge or off a table drops into nothing.
bbs_physics.config.general.world_above-c: How high over the scene ceilings and overhangs are collected.
bbs_physics.scene.title: Scene physics
bbs_physics.scene.none: No scene running — open a film
bbs_physics.scene.compute_tooltip: Record the rest of the film right now instead of waiting for the background catch-up. On a long film this stalls for a second or two.
bbs_physics.scene.reset_tooltip: Throw the recording away and start again from the opening frame.
bbs_physics.scene.gravity_tooltip: Blocks per second squared. Earth is 9.81; half of it reads as slow motion, zero is a space shot. It changes the whole recording, so the cache is recomputed.
bbs_physics.scene.steps_tooltip: How many times per tick the engine re-solves collisions. More is steadier for a stack of crates and costs more per step.
bbs_physics.scene.region_tooltip: How much of the world around the scene takes part. Past the edge there is no ground and a body falls forever.
bbs_physics.hud.tick: Physics: tick %s · %s bodies · recorded to %s of %s
bbs_physics.hud.not_recorded: Tick %s is not computed yet — showing plain animation
bbs_physics.hud.ghosts: Nothing marked up: %s — they fall through everything
bbs_physics.hud.outside: Past the scene's blocks: %s — there is no ground under them
bbs_physics.hud.lost: Lost by the solver: %s — pushed by an impossible force; the overlay cannot draw them
bbs_physics.forms.physics.title: Physics
bbs_physics.forms.physics.unmarked: Set up collision first — the Collision tab. Without it there is nothing for physics to take hold of: the form falls through everything and touches nothing.
bbs_physics.forms.body.mass_tooltip: Only matters when two moving bodies meet: in a vacuum everything falls alike.
bbs_physics.forms.body.type_tooltip: Active falls and gets shoved. Passive follows its keyframes and shoves others, but never moves itself — for scenery.
bbs_physics.forms.body.material_tooltip: Estimate the mass from a material: the volume of the marked shapes times its density. It stays an ordinary number afterwards.
bbs_physics.forms.body.title: Rigid body
bbs_physics.forms.body.authority_tooltip: 1 — the body follows its keyframes exactly and shoves everything aside. 0 — it is on its own, purely physics. In between it is pulled towards the animation by that much: it lags, sags and gives way. Animate it from 1 down to 0 on the timeline to let an object go.
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.title: Cloth
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.segments_x: Segments across — more means softer folds and a costlier simulation
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.segments_y: Segments down — more means softer folds and a costlier simulation
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.edge_tooltip: What the sheet holds on by. The held edge rides the animation; the rest hangs, flutters and catches on the world, bones and props.
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.self_collision_t: Other sheets will be able to land on this one. Jolt cannot solve soft against soft, so a grid of thin slabs is built to follow this sheet and stand in for it — real bodies in the scene, hence off by default. A sheet still cannot land on itself.
bbs_physics.forms.cloth.damping: Damping: how quickly the sheet stops swinging
bbs_physics.forms.collision.title: Collision
bbs_physics.forms.collision.mode_tooltip: By default a bone collides with nothing. "Auto from cubes" measures its own geometry. "Shapes by hand" switches itself on once you add a shape in the section below.
bbs_physics.forms.collision.shape_add: Add a shape — the bone moves from "auto from cubes" to hand markup
bbs_physics.forms.collision.auto_thresho: Bones smaller than this (in blocks) are skipped. Fingers and straps only cost contacts and change nothing on screen.
bbs_physics.forms.collision.auto_mark_to: Sets "auto from cubes" on every bone above the threshold. Bones you placed shapes on by hand are left alone — this is a draft, not an answer.
bbs_physics.forms.collision.fit_tooltip: Puts one box the size of what the form draws into the form's own slot. A block is measured from its real outline; anything else gets a block-sized box to drag from.
bbs_physics.forms.collision.context.name: Preset name...
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.title: Ragdoll
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.kind_tooltip: "Cone" is a joystick — shoulders, hips, the neck. "Hinge" is a door hinge — knees and elbows. "Welded" does not bend at all, which is how chest and belly become one piece. "No joint" attaches to nothing.
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.swing_tooltip: How far the bone may lean away from its rest direction, in any direction.
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.hinge_axis_too: The bone's local axis the hinge bends around. If a knee bends the wrong way, flip the angles' signs or the axis.
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.attach_tooltip: "Auto" is the marked ancestor in the bone tree, and when there is none (the standard player hangs everything off empty wrapper bones) — the nearest marked body by geometry. Pick a bone by hand when auto guesses wrong.
bbs_physics.forms.ragdoll.context.name: Preset name...
